analysis.title: Investor Positioning and Flows - Rates Vol Taking A Toll
key_insights: Equity positioning overall is resilient at modestly overweight levels (0.27sd, 60th percentile) despite the surge in rates volatility, and moved largely sideways this week.
Large-cap positioning is overweight (85th percentile) but not extreme, and is well below levels implied by the earnings boom. Small-cap positioning slipped to modestly underweight (43rd percentile).

Systematic strategies remain elevated (92nd percentile) and are vulnerable to higher equity vol. Discretionary positioning has fallen to below neutral (27th percentile in the headline, 29th percentile in the detail section).
The decline in discretionary equity positioning tracks the rise in rates vol (MOVE index correlation -62% since 2021). DB says rates vol, not the level of rates, is the key for equities.
Sector positioning is narrow. MCG & Tech (82nd percentile) is the only clear overweight, Energy is near neutral, and other cyclicals and defensives are at or below neutral.

The rotation into Tech has run a long way, with another 2pp of outperformance this week. The MCG & Tech ratio to the rest of the S&P 500 is approaching levels from which it has reversed several times, though it is not at the top of its long-run trend channel.
Vol control funds' equity allocation is at the 98th percentile. Capacity for further equity additions is limited and the flow backdrop is asymmetric, becoming less supportive if volatility rises.

CTA equity positioning declined this week but remains elevated (77th percentile), with US at 91st, Europe 79th, EM 76th and Japan 60th. Further additions depend more on falling volatility than on stronger trend signals.

CTAs remain extremely short bonds (US 11th percentile, Europe 12th percentile) and long the dollar (96th percentile). In commodities, gold is short (15th percentile) while copper (98th) and oil (78th) are strongly long.

Risk parity equity allocations dipped but remain elevated (73rd percentile). Bond allocations are below norms (33rd percentile), and commodity, REIT and inflation-hedge exposures are at 93rd-95th percentiles.

Options and sentiment: the call/put volume ratio fell this week but is still at the 82nd percentile, and S&P 500 3m skew rose. AAII bull-bear spread is at the 16th percentile, the fourth straight bearish week.

Weekly fund flows: equity funds took in $15.8bn after last week's outflows, but US funds had a second week of outflows (-$2.7bn). Bond funds took in $18.8bn, and money market funds lost $118.0bn, including a record European outflow of $38.5bn.
Sector fund flows: Tech took in $3.3bn, its largest weekly inflow in a month. Utilities took in $1.0bn, the largest YTD. Industrials had a second week of outflows (-$0.5bn).
Bond fund flows: government bond inflows of $10.8bn were the highest in four months, and muni inflows of $4.2bn were a record. IG moved to outflows (-$1.1bn), and HY and MBS each lost $1.4bn.
DB S&P 500 forecasts: 2026 target 8000, 2026 EPS $358, 2027 EPS $420.

Chart on the Tech rotation: the MCG & Tech ratio to the rest of the S&P 500 (log, trend growth 14.2% annualized, band +/- 10%), with the text saying it is approaching levels from which it has reversed several times.
Systematic strategies positioning vs S&P 500 1m realized vol (inverted), correlation -77%.
vol_and_positioning: Vol control funds' equity allocation is at the 98th percentile. Sell-off sensitivity increased but eased from earlier-week levels, and capacity for further equity additions is limited.
The systematic strategy positioning composite is correlated -77% with S&P 500 1m realized vol. Systematic positioning is at the 92nd percentile amid subdued equity vol.
S&P 500 3m skew (90%-110%) increased this week, and the call/put volume ratio (5d ma) fell but stays at the 82nd percentile.
Total net call volume (5d ma) is at the 98th percentile since 2010.
Blended large-cap mutual fund beta to the S&P 500 is low (1m rolling 23rd percentile, 3m rolling 16th percentile). Equity L/S hedge fund beta is high (1m 78th, 3m 93rd percentile).
A basket of the highest net call volume stocks from the prior week modestly underperformed this week, and the most shorted stocks also underperformed.
Futures: CTA bond shorts are extreme and dollar longs are elevated (96th percentile).

tension_points.bull_case: Aggregate positioning is steady at the 60th percentile, large caps are overweight at the 85th percentile but not extreme and below earnings-implied levels, and systematic strategies hold firm (92nd percentile) amid subdued equity vol.
tension_points.bear_case: Discretionary positioning has dropped to the 27th percentile as rates vol rose, small caps are cut below neutral, and systematic positioning is vulnerable to higher equity vol.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A rise in equity volatility would push systematic strategies and vol control funds (98th percentile) to sell, and the report says further equity additions depend on declining volatility.
